title: Unified Inference: V26 Product Overview, PRD, Design Specs, Roadmap & Pricing (2028-09)
author: Ava Patel
body:
Overview:

This document consolidates the product overview, high-level PRD, core design specifications, roadmap themes for the next 6 quarters, pricing & packaging notes, and the release notes for the Unified Inference V26 milestone (internal name: UI-V26). UI-V26 continues Redwood's thesis of making inference predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments with a focus on throughput determinism, unit-cost reduction, and improved private deployment ergonomics.

Purpose and audience:
- Purpose: Provide a single source-of-truth for engineering, product, solutions, and GTM teams for V26 scope, success metrics, rollout plan, and pricing changes.
- Audience: Product, Eng (Serving Runtime, Infra, Platform), SRE, Solutions/SE, Sales & Finance.

1) Executive summary:
- Primary goals: 1) Reduce per-token cost by 12-18% for typical PLG workloads via batching and quantization automation; 2) Improve 99th percentile inference latency on multi-tenant Hosted API by 15% at p95 throughput; 3) Ship a hardened Private deployment installer with simplified KMS/HSM integration and automated upgrade/rollback.
- Key user outcomes: Lower bill shock for customers, more reliable low-latency response for interactive features, faster on-prem adoption for regulated customers.

2) PRD (high level):
- Problem statements:
  1) Customers face variable per-token economics because runtime batching parameters and quantization profiles require manual tuning.
  2) Hosted customers see occasional latency spikes during short-term traffic bursts that affect interactive apps.
  3) Enterprise customers need an easier private deployment experience with opinionated defaults for KMS, VPC routing, and upgrades.

- Scope (V26):
  - Redwood Optimize: auto-profiled batching and quantization suggestions + one-click apply for Dedicated and Hosted.
  - Serving runtime: adaptive burst-aware scheduling and priority routing to reduce latency spikes.
  - Private deployment: new installer (airgap optional), default KMS provider templates (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault), automated DB migrations, and rollback hooks.
  - Console: cost-simulation sandbox and per-route cost guardrails for quotas and alerts.

- Non-goals:
  - Full workflow for model training or dataset management.
  - Replacing custom customer quantization profiles (we provide suggestions, customers can still upload).

- Success metrics (KPIs):
  - Unit cost reduction: median cost-per-generated-token across top-50 tenants down 12-18% within 90 days of rollout.
  - Latency: reduce Hosted API 99th-percentile latency by 15% at standard load profile.
  - Private installations: reduce median time-to-first-successful-upgrade by 50% vs V25.
  - Adoption: >40% of Dedicated customers opt-in to Redwood Optimize within 60 days.

- Stakeholders & ownership:
  - Product lead: Ava Patel
  - Eng owners: Runtime (Evan Brooks), Optimize (Sofia Morales), Private Deployments (Lina Rodriguez)
  - SRE: Michael Chen
  - Sales & GTM liaison: Priya Nair

3) Design specifications (summarized):

A. Adaptive batching & quantization automation
- Overview: Automatically derive batching window (ms) and target batch size by profiling request length distribution and model latency variance. Suggest quantization profiles (4-bit/8-bit) per-model and workload. Provide one-click application that deploys safe fallbacks.
- Components:
  - Profiler service (offline + continuous mode) that consumes traces and token histograms (owned by Optimize team).
  - Profiling outputs: preferred_batch_ms, preferred_batch_tokens, quant_profile_id.
  - Apply path: controller issues canary update to a model-serving pool with traffic split 5/95, monitors latency and token-level quality regressions via eval probe sets.
- Safety checks (must pass before apply):
  1) No regressions > 2% in BLEU/ROUGE or sentinel evals for configured eval sets.
  2) Latency tail increase < 5% on canary.
  3) If any check fails, automatic rollback and alert to oncall.

B. Burst-aware scheduling and priority routing
- Overview: Add a scheduling tier that dynamically reserves small pre-warmed slices of GPU capacity for latency-sensitive tenant requests (interactive plan) while allowing lower-priority batch inference to use background capacity.
- Config defaults:
  - interactive_reservation_pct = 8
  - background_preemption_threshold = 70%
  - priority_levels = ["high", "default", "low"]
- API/Config example (JSON):
  {
    "routing_policy": "latency_first",
    "interactive_reservation_pct": 8,
    "priority_defaults": {"high": 0.9, "default": 0.6, "low": 0.3}
  }
- Rollout technical notes:
  1) Begin with internal alpha on dedicated clusters, validate p99 improvement.
  2) Deploy to Hosted Canary region for subset of traffic.

C. Private deployment installer & ops improvements
- Features:
  - Installer supports: airgapped bundle, interactive CLI, unattended mode with manifest, and Terraform module for infra provisioning.
  - KMS templates: AWS/GCP/Azure; HSM integration guide included.
  - DB migrations: versioned migrations with dry-run and revert.
  - Health-checks: automated post-upgrade smoke tests and automatic rollback if core services fail.
- Upgrade flow (numbered):
  1) Upload/verify new bundle (sha256).
  2) Run dry-run migrations.
  3) Canary upgrade 2 nodes, run smoke tests 60s.
  4) Gradual ring expansion 2 -> 10 -> rest with health gates.
  5) Finalize and cleanup.

4) Roadmap & themes (Q4 2028 -> Q1 2029):
- Themes by quarter:
  - Q4 2028: Stabilize Optimize automation (profiler in continuous mode), Hosted latency SLO improvements, Private installer GA.
  - Q1 2029: Expand model catalog compatibility for quantization profiles, per-tenant simulation sandbox in Console, partner integrations for managed private deployments.
  - Q2 2029: Autoscaling policies for Dedicated with cost-SLO tradeoff UI, advanced evaluation hooks for semantic quality drift.

- Release milestones (dates are target):
  - Beta (Optimize + Private installer): 2028-10-15
  - GA release UI-V26: 2028-11-30
  - Post-GA minor: 2029-01-15 (first set of iterative improvements)

5) Pricing & packaging notes:
- Guiding principles: pricing changes should align with measurable unit-cost improvements customers receive and be optional for Dedicated/Private early adopters.
- Changes in V26:
  - Redwood Optimize auto-profiling: free trial for 30 days; paid as an add-on after trial priced as 5% of token spend savings credit (example: if Optimize lowered costs by $10k/month, customer billed $500/month). Billing is usage-based and reported in Console cost-simulator.
  - Hosted API: no base price change; customers who opt-in to Optimize receive discounted per-token rates for optimized routes (10% lower on generated tokens billed for routes under the Optimize policy).
  - Dedicated: Optimize is a paid add-on (annual or monthly commitment). Customers can trial in a sandbox cluster for 60 days.
  - Private: Professional Services uplift for installation and KMS/HSM integration; options for ongoing Optimize advisory retainers.

- Billing examples (text table):
  - Example 1: Mid-market app with $20k monthly token spend; after Optimize (-15% cost) savings $3k -> Optimize fee = $150/month.
  - Example 2: Startup with $2k monthly spend; after Optimize (-12%) savings $240 -> Optimize fee = $12/month (min charge $25/month applies).

6) Rollout plan & runbooks (high level):
- Staged rollout strategy:
  1) Internal alpha (eng + SE) on dedicated clusters — 3 weeks.
  2) Customer beta (invited tenants in Hosted Canary region + Dedicated trial customers) — 6 weeks.
  3) GA with gradual percent rollout and monitoring gates — 2 weeks rollout window with 24/7 oncall coverage.

- Monitoring gates & alerts (examples):
  - If canary latency p99 increases > 10% -> automatic rollback.
  - If quality eval regressions > 2% on sentinel sets -> rollback + block rollout.
  - If error budget burn rate > 1.5x -> pause rollout and engage SRE.

- Oncall runbook snippets:
  - Check canary dashboards: /dashboards/ui-v26-canary
  - Revert command (CLI):
    redwood-cli rollout rollback --deployment <id> --reason "canary-regression"
  - Escalation: notify Runtime oncall -> Product lead -> SRE manager.

7) Release notes (V26 GA — 2028-11-30):
- Major features:
  - Redwood Optimize: continuous profiler, automated batching/quantization suggestions, one-click canary apply.
  - Serving runtime: burst-aware scheduling with priority reservations.
  - Private deployment: GA installer with KMS templates, automated migrations, and rollback hooks.
- Improvements:
  - Hosted API latency: 15% p99 improvement in standard load tests.
  - Console: cost-simulation sandbox and per-route cost guardrails.
- Known issues (to be tracked post-GA):
  1) Rare spike in profiler memory usage observed on models > 25B during long traces (workaround: restart profiler pod; fix planned Q1 2029).
  2) In some airgapped installs, customers with very restrictive egress require manual CA import for KMS; add to installer docs.

8) Open risks & mitigation:
- Risk: Quality regressions after automated quantization. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, mandatory sentinel eval checks, and canary rollbacks.
- Risk: Billing confusion for Optimize fees. Mitigation: clear Console simulations, sample billing scenarios in invoices, and a dedicated billing FAQ page.

9) Implementation timeline & owners (summary table as text):
- Product: Ava Patel (overall)
- Runtime: Evan Brooks (adaptive scheduling)
- Optimize: Sofia Morales (profiler + suggestions)
- Private Deployments: Lina Rodriguez (installer & KMS)
- Console: Devansh Patel (cost-simulator)
- SRE: Michael Chen (rollout, monitoring gates)

10) Action items & next steps:
1) Complete end-to-end integration test for canary apply flow by 2028-09-25 (Optimize + Runtime teams).
2) Prepare customer-facing pricing FAQ and billing examples for Sales by 2028-10-01.
3) Run two internal game-days simulating canary regressions and rollback by 2028-10-05 (SRE + Runtime + Product).
4) Publish GA announcement draft and support playbook by 2028-11-10 (GTM + Product + Support).
